summary: Opens the browser's native file dialog on a signal and outputs the picked file plus its name, size and MIME type.
description: When the `open` (Open) signal fires, the node clicks a hidden HTML file input, showing the browser's native file dialog. When the user picks a file, the `file` output delivers the browser File object (the value upload nodes expect), the Metadata outputs update, and `success` fires. If the user cancels the dialog, nothing fires — there is no cancel event. The selection is reset after each pick, so choosing the same file again still triggers `success`. `acceptedFileTypes` maps to the file input's accept attribute; `capture` maps to the capture attribute, which on mobile devices requests a camera or microphone as the source.
whenToUse: Use it whenever the user must supply a file from their device — avatar upload, CSV import — typically firing `open` from a Button's `onClick` and passing `file` to an Upload File node. It is browser-only; there is no folder or multi-file selection.

ports.open: Signal; opens the file dialog. Must come from a user-initiated signal such as a click — browsers block programmatic file dialogs outside user gestures.
ports.acceptedFileTypes: String value; the accept attribute, e.g. 'image/*' or '.png,.csv'. Filters the dialog but is not validation — verify `type` if it matters.
ports.capture: String value; the capture attribute ('user' or 'environment'). On mobile, requests capturing from the front or rear camera instead of browsing files.
ports.file: Untyped value; the picked browser File object — wire this to Upload File.
ports.name: String value; the picked file's filename.
ports.sizeInBytes: Number value; the picked file's size in bytes.
ports.type: String value; the picked file's MIME type, e.g. 'image/png'.
ports.path: String value; read from the File object's path property, which standard browsers do not provide — usually undefined. Use `name` instead.
ports.success: Signal; fires after a file has been picked and all outputs are updated. Never fires on cancel.

patterns: Button `onClick` → `open`, then `file` → Upload File and `success` → the upload's trigger: the standard upload flow.
Latch `success` into a Boolean (value pinned true, `success` → Set) to reveal post-pick UI as a level.
antiPatterns: Treating `acceptedFileTypes` as a guarantee — users can often override the filter; check `type`/`sizeInBytes` before acting on the file.
